title: Harry Styles Dresses as NYC ‘Pizza Rat,’ Gets Jalen Brunson Tribute at Final MSG Residency Show
summary: The pop star marked the occasion with a Halloween tribute to one of the city's most infamous viral sensations.
contentText:
Harry Styles gave fans a memorable sendoff at his final Together, Together residency show at New York’s Madison Square Garden.

On Saturday (Oct. 31), the 32-year-old pop superstar wrapped up the second night — and 30th show of his residency — with Harryween, dressing as the city’s infamous Pizza Rat.

The “As It Was” singer took the stage in a furry brown onesie complete with oversized pink ears, a long tail and black sunglasses, while carrying a giant foam slice of pizza. The costume appeared to pay homage to the viral 2015 video of a rat dragging a slice of pizza down the stairs of a New York City subway station.

Styles’ backing band joined in the Halloween festivities, dressing as other NYC staples, including a hot dog and a taxi cab.

View this post on Instagram

The evening also featured a special tribute to Styles, with Madison Square Garden raising a commemorative banner to the arena’s rafters. New York Knicks captain and 2026 NBA Finals MVP Jalen Brunson presented the banner to the singer during the show. The Garden also unveiled a new “Defining Moments” exhibit on its sixth-floor, featuring memorabilia from Styles’ 10-week residency.

During the previous night’s Harryween show on Friday (Oct. 30), the Grammy winner opened the evening dressed as Elvis Presley, while his band and dancers dressed as different versions of Styles from throughout his career. He later changed into the outfit he wore for his 2010 X Factor audition and performed Stevie Wonder’s “Isn’t She Lovely,” the song that helped him advance to the next round of the competition at age 16.

Styles’ MSG run supported his fourth solo studio album, Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally. , which debuted at No. 1 on both the Billboard 200 and the Official U.K. Albums Chart.

Styles’ Together, Together tour will continue through August 2027 with a 25-date extension launching April 2 in Phoenix. The North American leg will include stops in Dallas, Los Angeles, Toronto, Atlanta and Chicago. The European leg begins July 2 in Berlin, with additional dates in Paris, Madrid, Rome and Dublin, before wrapping Aug. 28 with the third and final show at London’s Wembley Stadium.
